options.consequence: a set literal whose elements reference top-level variables or static fields initialized by StateTopic creations with literal names; an unresolved write set or scope is an unresolved_claim warning and the claim takes no part, as Spec §3.11 says

options.label: constant evaluation
options.consequence: generated registries use static final members, which are not constants, so most real claims would not resolve

chosen: set literal of declared state topics; else warning and left out
why: Spec §3.11: 'A write set the scan cannot resolve statically is reported as a warning and left to Layer 1'. topic-codegen@v1 generates static final members, so the rule reads declarations' initializers instead of constant values. An unresolved scope is treated like an unresolved write set because the scope check would otherwise misjudge the owner.

question: What source does a claim get when its source argument does not resolve (a parameter, a PageScope without route)?

options.label: stand-in named by the site
options.consequence: the claim keeps its place in single-writer and scope checks; reports and catalog's document show e.g. page:app/lib/cart_page.dart:42:10

options.label: leave the claim out with a warning
options.consequence: most PageScope claims, whose route is derived at run time, and every generic helper's claim escape the merge-time checks

chosen: stand-in named by the site
why: Spec §3.11 limits the warning to unresolvable write sets; a source only labels a writer, and flutter-binding@v1 G7 derives a page's route at run time by design. Close call: the signal against it would be the owner finding site-named sources in topics.md confusing.

question: What does the scan read (OQ-T2's residual: workspace AST scan, catalog IR plus AST claims, or both with the plugin surfacing verdicts)?

options.label: graph topologies plus own source walk
options.consequence: topologies from catalog's topology-graph.json via --graph, claims and topic declarations resolved from source by the recognizer catalog shares; the document's claims ignored so none counts twice; no dependency on OQ-T1's registration mechanism

options.label: the whole graph document
options.consequence: one graph exactly, but claim recognition and its warnings live only in catalog, and no recorded invocation could exercise the recognizer

options.label: build the graph in-process
options.consequence: one command for apps, but the scan inherits OQ-T1 (registration, constructor configuration, Flutter-importing libraries under dart run) and its fixtures could not be fixed now

options.label: AST-only topology scan
options.consequence: re-implements the DSL's meaning in the analyzer, cannot see state-bearing edges for self-reference

chosen: graph topologies plus own source walk
why: Spec §3.11 has the scan and the graph generator share infrastructure and Spec §6.5 has CI lint the catalog's static graph; topic-codegen@v1 already makes the graph document the seam and has catalog take its claims from this contract's recognizer. Reading only the document's topologies keeps the scan executable over hand-made documents in fixtures while the recognizer stays executable here. OQ-T2's third option (plugin surfacing verdicts) is not taken in v1.

question: What are the scan command's name, output format and exit codes?

options.label: scan, pipe-separated lines, 0/1/2
options.consequence: nidana_dart_codegen:scan prints {severity}|{code}|{location}|{message} lines, errors then warnings; exit 1 only for error lines, 2 for usage and unreadable or undecodable graphs

options.label: check, JSON report with a schema
options.consequence: easier for tools, but a schema, valid and invalid cases, and a less readable recording; the line form is already parseable

chosen: scan, pipe-separated lines, 0/1/2
why: 'workspace scan' is ADR-002's and the root's term, so the executable takes it. topic-codegen@v1's 0/1/2 convention is kept, but an undecodable graph exits 2, not 1, so that exit 1 always means the checks found a violation. The line form mirrors dart analyze --format=machine (one diagnostic per line, escaped separators). A JSON report is a compatible later addition.
evidence: topic-codegen@v1 generate and catalog exit codes

question: Must the scan report duplicate topology ids itself (S08's note)?

options.label: no, the document cannot hold them
options.consequence: catalog exits 1 on two unequal definitions with one id (topic-codegen@v1 G21) and the decoder rejects duplicate ids (topology-ir@v1 G21), so the scan's input never has them

options.label: yes, a duplicate_topology_id check
options.consequence: a check that can never fire on a decodable document

chosen: no, the document cannot hold them
why: S08's note applied to whatever builds the graph from definitions, which is catalog; the scan reads a decoded document.

question: How does the scan render a TopicRef's typeName, so that a claim and a topology writing one topic compare equal?

options.label: as the VM renders '$T'
options.consequence: equal to the analyzer's display string for interface, generic, nullable, enum, record and aliased types; function types render (String) => int

options.label: the analyzer's display string
options.consequence: a function-typed topic's claim would never meet the topology writing it (int Function(String) against (String) => int)

chosen: as the VM renders '$T'
why: Probe P1 compared both renderings for nine type forms on the pinned SDK; only function types differ. The graph document's TopicRefs come from the VM (topology-ir@v1, topic-model@v1 TopicRef).

question: How are recorded invocations laid out so that test directories exist and dart run works?

options.label: plugin cases: files/ is the package root; scan cases: packages under files/
options.consequence: follows ADR-001 item 7 literally (the plugin enabled in files/analysis_options.yaml, seven levels up to the root); scan cases keep files/ free of pubspec.yaml, because dart run from a pubspec directory runs an implicit pub get that writes a lockfile there

options.label: every case under files/app/
options.consequence: uniform, but enables the plugin outside files/analysis_options.yaml, against ADR-001 item 7's wording

chosen: plugin cases: files/ is the package root; scan cases: packages under files/
why: A plugin is honored only in the options at a package root (a probe with the options one level above the pubspec reported nothing), the test-directory exemption needs a package root, and a probe showed dart run creating .dart_tool and pubspec.lock in a nested package, which ADR-002 item 1 forbids.

question: Where must dart analyze run for the plugin to report?

options.label: at the enabling root or on files
options.consequence: the contract tells app CI to run dart analyze at the package or workspace root; the plugin cases run on '.'

options.label: any path
options.consequence: untrue on the pinned SDK: dart analyze lib reports no plugin diagnostic and exits 0

chosen: at the enabling root or on files
why: Probe P2: on one package, '.' and lib/app.dart report all four rules, lib reports nothing and exits 0. A CI step that analyzes a subdirectory would pass silently.

question: Frontmatter: kind, compatibility, producers, consumers, schema

options.label: cli, versioned, node ids, no schema
options.consequence: kind cli as the root matrix recommends; produced_by nidana.tooling, consumers nidana.integration with phase_ids provisional, as topic-codegen@v1; external consumers app CI (analyze and scan) and IDEs; recorded invocations are the artifact, and the graph documents are validated by topology-ir@v1's schema

options.label: cli plus a report schema
options.consequence: only useful with a JSON report, which v1 does not have

chosen: cli, versioned, node ids, no schema
why: Root contract matrix and ADR-001 item 7 (recorded invocations for cli); node ids stand until hsdd-reconcile confirms phase ids.

question: Which guarantees are not executable, and is stderr recorded?

options.label: three not-executable lines, no stderr
options.consequence: G9's no-write clause, G17's environment independence and G18 (catalog's use of the recognizer) are checked by nidana.tooling's gates; stderr text stays out of the contract, as topic-codegen@v1 keeps it

options.label: record stderr
options.consequence: pins usage texts and FormatException messages that the decoder's implementation words

chosen: three not-executable lines, no stderr
why: ADR-001 item 7 compares streams and exit codes only, so file writes and catalog's output are out of its reach; usage and decoder messages are implementation text.
evidence: topic-codegen@v1 generate (stderr not part of the contract)

question: With all nine root contracts written, which accumulated follow-ups run now, before the runtime and tooling decompositions, and which wait?

options.label: ADR and contract touches now; root prose in one root refresh after stage 5
options.consequence: Five small steps now (ADR-001, ADR-003, navigation-api@v1, bus-api@v1, topic-codegen@v1) so the decompositions read consistent governance; root D1's check table, OQ2, OQ5 and the embedded child summaries are fixed once, after both mid-level decompositions have also touched the root.

options.label: Everything now, including a root refresh
options.consequence: The root is refreshed twice, because each mid-level decomposition rewrites its embedded summary in the root anyway.

options.label: Defer everything to reconcile
options.consequence: The decompositions would read ADR-001 wording that no longer matches the contracts (the 'live topology builder', the fixture directories its structure set does not name) and ADR-003 without its link to topology-dsl@v1.

chosen: ADR and contract touches now; root prose in one root refresh after stage 5
why: The mid-level decompositions inject ADRs and cut against contracts, so those should be consistent first. Root prose is read by nobody downstream before reconcile and is rewritten by the decompositions anyway. Left out on purpose: a nidana-declared Sensitive annotation (nidana-checks@v1 lists it as a later candidate, and apps can declare their own class) and the sensitivity keyword list (not configurable through analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18). ADR-001's file cases with expected exit codes go to the ADR-001 step to decide, since it changes the ADR's decision rather than its wording.

question: Decide whether this is an in-place amendment of the accepted ADR or a superseding ADR, and record why.

options.label: amend in place
options.consequence: Every item number and every Governed by link stays; the amended text becomes what hsdd-config injects; the original text survives in git (1fc3a48) and the change is recorded in a dated ## Amendments section.

options.label: supersede with ADR-004
options.consequence: New file with supersedes: [ADR-001] and ADR-001 set to superseded; Governed by moves in seven node specs and nine contracts, and the contract bodies' many 'ADR-001 item N' citations point at a superseded ADR until separate contract steps rewrite them.

chosen: amend in place
why: No change reverses an item: the kinds, the sets, their pass rules for existing fixtures and the replay tool stay, and all nine contracts as written still pass the amended rules (structure-output.txt S1). Superseding exists so a replaced decision is not injected as binding; here the binding text simply becomes the amended one, so a superseding ADR would cost a touch of every node spec and contract for no change in what binds. Signal that would have changed it: any change that made an existing fixture fail or removed a set, which would be a new decision rather than an amendment.

question: How should item 4's cross-contract binding example, and the matching Consequences bullet, read now that topology-dsl@v1 has no live builder?

question: Which directories may a fixture tree hold besides the named sets, and what does the structure set do with them?

options.label: data directories listed in Validation; structure fails on any other entry

options.consequence: Mechanical, but every new data directory needs an ADR change.

why: It is the only option that catches a misspelt set directory without centralizing names. Both existing data directories are already listed as '- {dir}: `hsdd/contract/fixture/{slug}/{dir}/`, ...'; the prototype check passed all nine contracts as written and reported a misspelt rejcet/ and an unlisted goldens/. Item 2 now also says the replay never analyzes input trees, expected trees or data directories, which topic-codegen@v1's expected/topics.g.dart (imports of a stand-in app) needs.

question: How does item 3's coverage rule count the schema set, the file replay and recorded invocations, whose files carry no G{n}?

options.label: declared in Validation in the forms the contracts use

why: topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 already declare coverage exactly this way, and structure already parses Validation for bindings and not-executable lines. The prototype parsed every declaration in the nine contracts and found every guarantee covered or not executable, and reported a removed covers clause and a case with no row. The schema clause is optional (topology-ir@v1's schema bullet covers nothing that behavior cases do not). The {ids} form, ids and 'G{a} to G{b}' ranges joined by ', ' or ' and ', matches every cell and header written so far. question: Item 3 and item 4 give one form each, '// covers: G{n}' and '- not executable: G{n}, ...'; contracts also wrote two-id reject headers and not-executable lines for part of a guarantee. Admit them or make contracts split guarantees?

question: S15 proposed extending item 6 so a file contract can carry several input/expected cases, including cases with an expected exit code (making topic-codegen@v1's G2, G14 and G19 executable). Does this belong in v1?

options.label: not in v1
options.consequence: No change; G2, G14 and G19 stay with nidana.tooling's gates, written by phases after the producer, and nidana.integration's --all never replays them. Adding cases later is a compatible change.

options.label: item 6 case directories

options.consequence: One command runner and one tree comparison, composed; topic-codegen@v1's single input/expected pair is untouched; about thirty lines in the replay tool's cli set; topic-codegen@v1 gains sixteen case directories at its next touch.

chosen: item 7 gains {output} and expected/; file contracts may carry recorded invocations
why: It makes G14 fully and G2 and G19 in part executable before the producer exists, replayed at every gate and by nidana.integration's --all, at the cost of a small addition to a tool not yet written. Composing item 7's runner with item 6's comparison avoids a second case layout. The prototype ran sixteen candidate cases (no graph, undecodable graph, four usage errors, the ten rejected/ documents) against S15's stand-in generator, all passing, and four seeded defects (accepting a rejected document, a changed catalog, a page written without a graph, a wrong exit code) each failed. The diagnostic form of G19 and G2's valid/ and invalid/ halves stay not executable: stderr text is not part of topic-codegen@v1, and one case per invalid/ document would be 53 directories. Close call: the signal that would have favored 'not in v1' is nidana.model's first phase overflowing its Phase Equivalent with the replay tool.

hsdd/contract/topic-codegen.md (generate command, G2, G14, G18, G19)

question: Item 6 does not say a file contract may carry a schema and valid/ and invalid/ cases for its input format, which topic-codegen@v1 does.

question: Item 10 runs every set but behavior in full at every producing phase, and --guarantee restricts only behavior cases; how do the file and cli sets gate a node that delivers a generator or a checker over several phases?

options.label: --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations by declared ids

options.consequence: Phase plans would need --set exclusions the ADR does not provide for, and phase planning cannot change an ADR (governance is read-only then), so the gap would surface as a stop.

chosen: --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations by declared ids
why: Not in the step's list; found while amending item 3. With coverage now declared per case, the restriction is well defined, and closing it now costs a sentence in a tool not yet written rather than a later ADR touch during nidana.tooling's phase planning. The subset rule mirrors behavior's cumulative delivery. hsdd/contract/nidana-checks.md (Validation table: plugin and scan cases)

question: S17 went beyond the listed changes: it extended item 7 so a file contract may carry recorded invocations with expected exit codes (the item 6 option), and extended items 9 and 10 so --guarantee restricts file replays and recorded invocations and producing phases run file and cli sets restricted like behavior. Keep these, or limit the amendment to the listed wording fixes?

options.label: Keep them
options.consequence: topic-codegen@v1's G2, G14 and G19 become executable through recorded invocations in S21; nidana.tooling's producing phases can replay only the guarantees delivered so far, as api contracts already do.

options.consequence: Those three guarantees stay not executable, and every producing phase of nidana.tooling replays every file and cli case, including ones for guarantees not yet built.

chosen: Keep them
why: Each extension removes an asymmetry between api contracts and file or cli contracts rather than adding new machinery: the replay tool already runs recorded invocations for cli contracts, and restricting by guarantee is how behavior already works. Phase planning cannot amend an ADR, so the restriction has to be settled before the tooling phases are planned. The prototype in docs/auto-run/experiments/file-invocations/ shows all nine contracts still pass the amended structure check.

question: From S09 the orchestrator stamped its own decisions (DEC-186, 187, 193, 234, 246, 310) and the S10 to S16 run lines with local time (UTC+7) labelled as UTC, about seven hours late. The ledger is append-only. How is it corrected?

options.label: Rewrite the affected lines

options.label: Publish a correction file and guard the tool
options.consequence: The ledger stays append-only; docs/auto-run/timestamp-corrections.md gives each affected entry its commit-time bounds; ledger.mjs now rejects any time later than the clock, so the error cannot recur silently.

chosen: Publish a correction file and guard the tool
why: The decision schema says ledger lines are never edited or removed, and the owner's review is pinned to them. The true times are recoverable from git commit times, which the machine clock wrote, so a correction file loses nothing. The cause was hand-written stamps after a date-change notice that reported the local date; every stamp now comes from date -u.

question: Does topology-dsl@v1 belong in ADR-003's affects, with the matching Governed by on the contract?

options.label: Add topology-dsl@v1
options.consequence: ADR-003 affects gains topology-dsl@v1 and the contract header reads Governed by: [ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003]. hsdd-config then injects ADR-003's Decision and Consequences into every phase that consumes topology-dsl@v1, nidana.tooling phases included.

options.label: Leave affects as it is
options.consequence: The contract cites ADR-003 items 3 and 4 in G6, G22, G23 and its Live interpretation, but a phase that consumes topology-dsl@v1 without bus-api@v1 never receives the decision those guarantees depend on, and the bidirectional linking rule is broken in spirit.

chosen: Add topology-dsl@v1
why: Applying the S06 test: ADR-003 constrains guarantees consumers of topology-dsl@v1 rely on. G6 (no scheduler argument, item 4), G22 (live switchMap listens to the next inner without waiting on the cancel future, item 3) and G23 (time combinators timed exactly by the implementation's clock, item 4) are what app topology tests and nidana.runtime's live implementation build against, and Live interpretation steps 5 and 6 cite items 2 to 4. S05 left the contract out because the live builder was then to be bus-api@v1's; S07 moved the live semantics of every combinator into topology-dsl@v1 and left bus-api@v1 the activation entry point, so S05's premise no longer holds. The injection cost to nidana.tooling is small: that node also consumes bus-api@v1, which already carries ADR-003, so only a tooling phase naming topology-dsl@v1 without bus-api@v1 gains the ADR. Inserted before bus-api@v1 to follow the root contract matrix order that ADR-001's affects uses.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topology-dsl.md (G6, G22, G23; Live interpretation 5 and 6; Boundary)
hsdd/contract/bus-api.md (opening paragraph: Bus.activate interprets a TopologyPlan as topology-dsl@v1's Live interpretation states)
.agents/skills/hsdd-config/SKILL.md (Decisions: ADRs a contract's Governed by names, and ADRs whose affects names it)

question: Does topic-model@v1 belong in ADR-003's affects, re-testing the S06 orchestrator decision against the contract as it now stands?

options.label: Add topic-model@v1
options.consequence: hsdd-config injects ADR-003 into every phase that consumes topic-model@v1, which is nearly every phase of the tree, for obligations that bind only the producer.

options.label: Leave topic-model@v1 out
options.consequence: ADR-003 keeps reaching the producer through nidana.model; the contract keeps citing item 8 in G12 and G25 and item 9 in prose.

G12 (envelope fields, none defaulted) and G25 (no clock, no timer, no id, no I/O) cite item 8 but bind only nidana_dart_contracts, whose producer nidana.model ADR-003 already governs; the consumer side of item 8 (stamp from the provider clock) lands on nidana.runtime and navigation-api@v1, both governed. G5 (no dispatcher hint) cites Spec §3.6 and §11.1 only; item 9 motivates it in prose, and ADR-003's Consequences leave the question to topic-model@v1 as OQ-M3 rather than constrain it. The S06 signal, a consumer-side obligation from ADR-003 on topic-model values, has not appeared.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md (G5, G12, G25, and the prose before G5 and in the observer section)

question: Does topology-ir@v1 belong in ADR-003's affects?

question: Does topic-codegen@v1 belong in ADR-003's affects?

options.consequence: ADR-003 is injected into codegen consumers' phases; it would also imply nidana.tooling, its producer, is governed, which affects does not name.

question: How is the in-place change to an accepted ADR's affects recorded?

options.label: Dated Amendments line
options.consequence: A new ## Amendments section at the end, in S17's form for ADR-001, says what changed, why the accepted text left it out, and the outcome for every other contract. hsdd-config never injects it, so phase contexts are unchanged.

options.label: Frontmatter change only
options.consequence: The file stays as accepted apart from affects; the reason lives only in git history and this report.

chosen: Dated Amendments line
why: An accepted ADR changed after acceptance should say so in the file, as ADR-001 does since S17, and the step asked for an amendment line when anything changes. The Amendments section is outside Decision and Consequences, so no phase context grows. status stays accepted and date stays 2026-10-17; the amendment carries 2026-10-17, the UTC date of this step's decision timestamps. Not a supersession: the decision did not change.

question: Does the new link need a sentence in ADR-003's Decision or Consequences?

question: ADR-003 item 8 says no nidana package calls DateTime.now(), constructs a Stopwatch directly, or creates a timer or microtask outside a provider zone; read literally it covers nidana_dart_codegen and nidana_dart_lint, yet nidana.tooling is not in ADR-003's affects. Read item 8 as binding only the governed nodes, add nidana.tooling to affects, or narrow item 8's wording?

options.label: Add nidana.tooling to affects
options.consequence: One more hsdd-adr step; every tooling phase receives ADR-003's long Decision for a rule that its packages, which run no bus, have no reason to break.

options.label: Narrow item 8 now
options.consequence: An amendment for a case no artifact exercises.

chosen: Read it as binding the governed nodes
why: The tooling packages run no bus and need no clock: topic-codegen@v1 G17 already forbids anything non-deterministic in generated output, and the scan and plugin are analyses. ADR-003 reaches tooling phases through the contracts they consume. The signal that would change this: a tooling phase plan that needs time.

question: How does the contract state the rejection of a DeepLink published to nav.resolved-intent that bus-api@v1 G40 now gives: as a clause of G1, as a new guarantee, or as reject lines alone?

options.label: extend G1 with a publish clause
options.consequence: No new id; the existing G1 reject library already covers G1, so the new lines are covered by its header; G1 reads as one invariant, no DeepLink after resolution, over this contract's declarations and the publish paths onto its resolved-intent topic.

options.label: new guarantee G28 with its own reject library
options.consequence: A separately restrictable id, but one invariant split across two ids, and a second reject library for the same misuse.

options.label: reject lines only, G1 text unchanged
options.consequence: The fixture would pin a rejection no guarantee states, and Refinement 9's old text scoping G1 to this contract's own declarations would contradict the fixture.

chosen: extend G1 with a publish clause
why: The step names it a G1 reject line, and G1 already states the invariant. Refinement 9 scoped G1 to this contract's own declarations only because bus-api@v1's publish then let the call compile; with G40 that reason is gone, so the scope widens to what G1 always meant. A separate id buys nothing here because reject sets run unrestricted at every producing gate (ADR-001 item 10). Signal that would have changed my mind: a phase needing to deliver or restrict the publish clause separately from the rest of G1.

question: Which publish paths does the new reject coverage exercise: the Publisher call S13 probed (P19), or both publish paths G40 types?

options.label: Publisher.publish only
options.consequence: One line, exactly S13's probe P19; Bus.publish's rejection would be stated in G1 but unpinned.

options.label: both Bus.publish and Publisher.publish
options.consequence: Two lines; every path G1's clause names is pinned; the Bus.publish line needed its own confirmation (probe Q02).

chosen: both Bus.publish and Publisher.publish
why: G40 types both and G1's clause names both, so a fixture for one leaves half the clause unpinned. Q02 shows Bus.publish reports could_not_infer alone, like the Publisher line. They live in the existing G1 library rather than a new one, because ADR-001 item 4 groups reject fixtures per guarantee or per misuse, and this is the same misuse (a DeepLink where a resolved intent is required).

question: Refinement 8: keep this contract's own reading of bus-api@v1 G22 and G34 and add citations, or replace the reading with what G22 and G34 now state?

options.label: keep the reading, add citations
options.consequence: Two texts of the same rule, this contract's reading and bus-api@v1's guarantees, which can drift; the note that bus-api@v1's fixtures do not pin it would be false and would have to go anyway.

options.label: cite G22 and G34 as stated, history to Versioning
options.consequence: One definition, owned by bus-api@v1; Refinement 8 keeps why G14 and G24 depend on it and the evidence that a runtime without it drops a deep link; the history moves to the Versioning touch line.

chosen: cite G22 and G34 as stated, history to Versioning
why: Read side by side, bus-api@v1 G22 (connection before activate returns; connection-caused publishes from a provider-zone microtask) and G34 (every topology activated before start() connected when start() delivers the queue, even with nothing run between; the queue reaching those reads in its order) state the reading clause for clause. A second definition is the fork the skill warns against. G14 and G24 now cite G22 and G34 directly, and G24's 'as Refinement 8 reads them' became '(Refinement 8)'. Signal that would have changed my mind: any clause of the old reading that G22 or G34 did not state.

question: Refinement 9: does the contract say that explicit type arguments still let a DeepLink onto nav.resolved-intent, or leave it implicit in 'with its type arguments inferred'?

options.label: state the residual
options.consequence: One sentence and a probe line (Q08); G1's 'impossible by construction' is not over-read; matches G40's own residual sentence.

options.label: leave it implicit
options.consequence: Shorter, but a reader of G1 could take the publish clause to cover publish<NavIntent, DeepLink>, which compiles.

chosen: state the residual
why: G40 states the same residual for its own guarantee, and Q08 confirms publish<NavIntent, DeepLink>(NavigationTopics.resolvedIntent, DeepLink(uri)) compiles on the stand-in. Refinement 9 keeps the earlier TypeError history, which bus-api@v1's Versioning cites as 'navigation-api@v1 Refinement 9', so that cross-reference stays true.

question: The Validation bullet on the Flutter binding of the executor suite: name the file flutter-binding@v1 wrote only, or also the order in which its executor constructs and pumps?

options.label: path only
options.consequence: Least duplication with flutter-binding@v1's Validation; the harness description here stays silent on an order the real binding fixes.

options.label: path and construct-before-pump order
options.consequence: One more clause repeated from flutter-binding@v1's Validation (drift risk if that binding changes), but this contract's description of what the binding supplies matches the file it names.

chosen: path and construct-before-pump order
why: S14 records that flutter-binding@v1's binding constructs the executor before pumping its WidgetsApp, where the stand-in binding of S12 pumped first, and that both orders pass. The bullet already repeated the binding's settle and elapse; adding the order keeps it accurate to the named file at the cost of one clause. The stand-in sentence in the last Validation bullet now says the named binding replaces it. Close call: if flutter-binding@v1's binding were expected to change its order, path only would be the better choice.

question: Is the touch compatible within v1, or does G1's new clause make it breaking?

options.label: compatible within v1
options.consequence: Version kept; a Versioning line records the touch; consumers change nothing.

options.label: breaking, draft v2
options.consequence: A migration note and a second version for a clause that rejects nothing bus-api@v1 does not already reject.

options.label: run-stop-candidate
options.consequence: Only if an existing fixture or consumer fixture failed against the amended stand-in.

chosen: compatible within v1
why: No declaration changed, no guarantee was removed or weakened, no id moved. The clause adds no rejection of its own: bus-api@v1 G40 already rejects the call, so no code that compiled after S13 stops compiling, which is this contract's Versioning rule for a compatible change (a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass). The fixtures at 6843dc2, the amended fixtures, and flutter-binding@v1's executor binding all pass against the stand-in (B.1 to B.5, A.1 to A.5); the fixture diff is the one reject file (T2). Taken after the first full run of the experiment.

question: Is the widened-reference guarantee a new G41 or a sharpening of an existing guarantee (G6 or G7)? ADR-001 item 3: never renumber or reuse ids.

options.label: new G41
options.consequence: Its own id: case names begin 'G41', a phase restricts --guarantee bus-api/G41, and G6 and G7 keep their scope (lazy creation, name uniqueness). Costs one more id.

options.label: sharpen G7
options.consequence: G7 already says equal declarations share one subject, so a widened reference arguably falls under it; but G7 would grow from a naming rule into an access-typing rule covering reads, writes and writers, and --guarantee G7 would pull in six unrelated cases.

chosen: new G41
why: The new content (what each operation returns through a widened reference, writes, writers, topology reads) is more than G7's naming rule, and a separate id keeps --guarantee restrictions precise. bus-api@v1 Versioning lists a new guarantee that existing fixtures pass as compatible.

question: Which read-side operations does G41 cover, and what does each return through a widened reference?

options.label: every read, typed by the reference
options.consequence: observe returns a Stream<R> of the same payloads with G17's first values and G16's dedup; getCurrentValue the same value; getBufferedValues an unmodifiable List<R> of the same values; a topology read, its connection included, the same values; an observer receives topic.ref, the same through every reference. Needs a registry whose subject does not take the first access's type argument.

options.label: observe and getCurrentValue only
options.consequence: Covers S14's probe pair, which is what flutter-binding@v1's state widget does, but leaves replay buffers and topology reads order-dependent, so the next generic caller finds the same TypeError elsewhere.

chosen: every read, typed by the reference
why: Spec §3.2 gives one backing subject per topic per bus, created on first runtime access, whatever reaches it; flutter-binding@v1's widgets read through getCurrentValue, getBufferedValues and observe at whatever type argument their call site gives; a topology factory can hold widened references. Every read failed on the S13 stand-in in some order, and all of them pass on the patched one.

question: Does G41 cover writes through a widened reference (Bus.publish, Publisher.publish, writer and StateWriter.publish, a topology sink), and what about the envelope's type argument and a value outside the topic's value type?

options.label: include writes of a value of the value type; leave the envelope's type argument and off-type values outside
options.consequence: A widened publish is delivered as the same publish at the value type, to recorders, observers, subscriptions and reads at either type. Its envelope is a MessageEnvelope<R> (P2), so bus-testing@v1 G16's envelopesOf, typed by the topic and identical to the delivered envelopes, cannot return it: a gap that exists whatever G41 says, now reachable in both orders, left for a bus-testing@v1 touch.

options.label: exclude writes from G41
options.consequence: No interaction with bus-testing@v1 is stated here, but G41 would narrow what the delivery rule and G13 already say of every publish, a widened one included (G40 lets a generic caller publish without type arguments), and generic shell code that writes stays order-dependent.

options.label: include writes and pin the envelope at the topic's value type
options.consequence: Closes the bus-testing@v1 gap and allows a publish-time value check, but no runtime can build a MessageEnvelope<int> from a MultiWriterTopic<Object?> over topic-model@v1's public API (P3: valueType is a Type, with == only); it needs a type-capturing member on the Topic family, a topic-model@v1 amendment this step cannot write.

chosen: include writes of a value of the value type; leave the envelope's type argument and off-type values outside
why: Including keeps every existing statement about publishes true and makes them hold in either order; pinning the envelope is not implementable today; excluding would narrow existing text. The off-type value is the same covariance gap G40 already leaves outside for explicit type arguments. Close call against exclusion: if the owner reads Spec §4.2 strictly (every write at the declared type) and wants nidana-checks to flag widened publishes as it flags explicit type arguments, exclusion plus a lint would be cleaner; if a consumer needs typed envelopes of widened publishes, request topic-model@v1's type-capturing member and extend G41 compatibly.

question: How does the registry key and type a subject so the order of first access does not matter (topic-model@v1's valueType)?

options.label: key by name, compare topic values, store at Object?, convert at each access
options.consequence: The subject registers the topic value of the creating access; G7 compares topic values, valueType among them; payloads and buffers are held at Object? and each access converts at its own type argument, which is always a supertype of the value type, so the conversion is sound for every value of the value type. An off-type value is not detected at publish.

options.label: type the subject by the first access's type argument
options.consequence: The S13 stand-in's design: fails in both orders with a _Cell<Object?> cast to _Cell<int> or a StreamController<Object?> added to a Set<StreamController<int>> (P1, T7).

options.label: type the subject at the value type through a type witness
options.consequence: Typed subjects, typed envelopes and publish-time value checks, but needs a topic-model@v1 member that calls back generic code with the value type; topic-model@v1 has none today.

chosen: key by name, compare topic values, store at Object?, convert at each access
why: Spec §4.3's bus-level check compares the type a topic was declared with, and topic-model@v1 G7 already compares valueType, which a widened reference does not change; P3 shows a Type supports == only, so nothing can be instantiated at the value type from a widened reference. G41 states only the observable part (keyed by name, compared by topic values, never by a reference's type argument); the storage representation is nidana.runtime's.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md G7, G8 and the TopicRef paragraph
docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-widened/ (P1, P3, T5, T7, T8 collision defect)

question: What does G20's 'returns the same handle on every call' mean once writer is reachable through a widened reference?

options.label: same handle per type argument
options.consequence: G20 reads 'on every call with the same type argument (G41)'. Implementable in both orders (writers kept per topic and type argument); every existing case still holds; identity across type arguments is no longer promised.

options.label: keep 'every call'
options.consequence: Unimplementable in the widened-first order: the StateWriter<Object?> made first cannot be returned as the StateWriter<int> a later call asks for (T7: StateWriter<Object?> is not a subtype of StateWriter<int>), so G41 and G20 would contradict each other.

options.label: exclude writer through a widened reference from G41
options.consequence: G20 untouched, but its 'every call' stays unimplementable in that order, and generic code that writes a state topic must obtain the writer at the value type.

chosen: same handle per type argument
why: The old wording cannot be met across type arguments by any runtime over topic-model@v1's public API, no fixture or contract compares writers across type arguments (the G20 case compares two typed calls), and the experiment's seeded defect (writers per topic only) fails exactly the G41 writer case. It rewords an existing guarantee, so an owner would have been asked.

question: How does For static analysis cite nidana-checks@v1 G5, which adds top-level and static getters to the global-accessor definition?

options.label: restate G5's set and cite G5
options.consequence: One definition that matches the check, readable without opening nidana-checks@v1; a one-sentence copy that could drift if G5 changes.

options.label: keep the narrower definition and add that G5 also reports getters
options.consequence: Two definitions that disagree in one paragraph.

options.label: replace the definition by a bare reference to G5
options.consequence: No copy, but a reader of bus-api@v1 must open another contract to know what the term means.

chosen: restate G5's set and cite G5
why: The paragraph exists so the checks have one definition of what they recognize; the restated set is G5's own wording in substance, and the citation names the owner of the check. No guarantee of this contract changes.
evidence: hsdd/contract/nidana-checks.md G5 and the global_bus_accessor row

question: Where is the term 'widened reference' defined?

options.label: a Delivery rules bullet
options.consequence: The section that defines the terms the guarantees use; G41 stays one statement; the term can be cited by later guarantees.

options.label: inline in G41
options.consequence: Self-contained guarantee, but a longer one, and a later guarantee would redefine the term.

chosen: a Delivery rules bullet
why: The section's own sentence says it defines the terms the guarantees use; consistent terminology across guarantees. No evidence beyond the contract's structure.

question: Where do the G41 cases live, and how is 'either order' exercised?

options.label: six cases in bus_api_conformance.dart, each running both orders on fresh buses
options.consequence: The existing binding nidana_dart_runtime_test.dart runs them; Validation changes only its coverage line; each case fails if either order fails, and its reason string names the order.

options.label: a separate conformance library and binding
options.consequence: A second harness and a second binding to list in Validation and run in every gate, for cases that need nothing the existing harness lacks.

chosen: six cases in bus_api_conformance.dart, each running both orders on fresh buses
why: ADR-001 item 4 keeps one conformance library per subject; the helpers take widened references as generic shell code does, so inference gives each call the type argument Object?. One case per surface: state reads, replay reads, event publishes with observers, writers, a topology over widened references, and the collision check.

question: S20 leaves three compatible follow-ups in contracts other than bus-api@v1: bus-testing@v1 G16 (envelopesOf and payloadsOf throw a TypeError on an envelope published through a widened reference), the 'same writer on every later call' wording of stub in bus-testing@v1 G18 and flutter-binding@v1 G17 (the per-type-argument problem G20 had), and an editorial note in nidana-checks@v1 that still describes the older global-accessor definition. Run three more touch steps now, or route them to the producing nodes' phase planning?

options.label: Three more touch steps now
options.consequence: The contracts read consistently before decomposition, at the cost of three steps, each of which can surface further cross-contract follow-ups, as the last five did.

options.label: Route to the producers' phase planning as amend entries
options.consequence: nidana.runtime's and nidana.flutter's phase plans, and nidana.tooling's, emit amend entries for their own contracts, which reconcile folds in; the touch batch ends at S21; the follow-ups are named in those steps' prompts so none is lost.

chosen: Route to the producers' phase planning as amend entries
why: Each item is a producer-side semantic of a contract whose producer has not been planned yet, which is what hsdd-phase-plan's amend entry exists for: 'a guarantee or semantic this plan settled for a contract this node owns'. None blocks a decomposition: the runtime decomposition reads S20's registry notes, and nothing consumes these three wordings before the producer plans. Ending the batch here also stops a pattern in which each touch raised the next. The signal that would change this: a decomposition step that needs one of these settled to draw its children.

question: Does rejected/ move into the generate-rejected-* recorded invocations (S17's recommendation), stay and be duplicated into them, or stay as the one copy that the cases name by path?

options.label: move into files/
options.consequence: one copy, each case self-contained; G2's text ('every rejected/ document') and its gate note must be reworded, the - rejected: data-directory bullet goes, ADR-001 item 9's example (topic-codegen@v1's rejected/ documents) goes stale, and the schema prototype that validates the parsable rejected/ documents must look in invocation/ instead

options.label: keep rejected/ and copy into files/
options.consequence: no wording change, but two copies of ten documents that structure does not compare, so they can drift

options.label: keep rejected/ and name it by path
options.consequence: one copy; G2's text, the data-directory bullet, ADR-001 item 9's example and the schema prototype stay as they are; each case is args and exit_code only, running from the workspace root (ADR-001 item 7) and naming rejected/{name}.yaml, as generate-no-graph names input/topics.yaml; a case's input lives outside its case directory

chosen: keep rejected/ and name it by path
why: It is the only option with one copy that changes no guarantee wording and leaves ADR-001's text true. ADR-001 item 7 says a case without files/ runs from the workspace root, and item 9 lets cases read a data directory by a path from the root, so the cases are legal as written. Every rejected document's content is kept byte for byte, in place. A missing document fails its case loudly with exit 2 (experiment E6). The signal that would have favored moving: a replay tool that runs each case from an isolated copy of its case directory rather than inside the workspace.

question: Do generate-graph-undecodable and generate-usage-output-is-a-file hold their inputs in files/ as copies (S17's design), or name topology-ir@v1's invalid/format_v2.json and input/topics.yaml in place?

options.label: copies in files/
options.consequence: two copies of input/topics.yaml and one of topology-ir@v1's invalid/format_v2.json; the case cannot be broken by a rename in another contract's fixture tree

options.label: name them in place
options.consequence: no copies, but topic-codegen@v1's replay then depends on a file of topology-ir@v1's fixture tree, which that contract may rename within its own version

chosen: copies in files/
why: The contract already copies across contracts rather than referencing (input/topology-graph.json is a copy of topology-ir@v1's valid/checkout.json), and a reference across fixture trees couples two contracts' touches. Naming rejected/ in place differs because it is this contract's own tree. The copies of input/topics.yaml only need to stay accepted, which E1 shows. Close call; the signal that would have changed it: a structure check that verifies cross-contract fixture paths.

question: Record exactly the sixteen cases S17 listed, or add a usage case for a missing graph file?

options.label: the sixteen of S17
options.consequence: matches the cases S17's experiment ran; a generator that treats a missing --graph file as an undecodable graph (exit 1) passes every case

options.label: add generate-usage-missing-graph
options.consequence: seventeen cases; the boundary between the exit table's 'a missing input file' (2) and 'the graph document does not decode' (1) is replayed

chosen: add generate-usage-missing-graph
why: The exit-code table already puts a missing input file at 2 and an undecodable graph at 1, so the case adds coverage without adding a rule, and a missing graph is the one input on that boundary that the sixteen leave out. In the experiment, the seeded defect missing-graph-exits-1 passes all sixteen of S17's cases and the file replay, and fails only this case (E5).

question: Make G2 executable in full by recording generate over every valid/ and invalid/ document too, or only over rejected/, with a part line for the rest?

options.label: rejected/ only, part line for the rest
options.consequence: ten rejection cases; G2's acceptance of valid/, rejection of invalid/ and its builder half stay with nidana.tooling's gates

options.label: add 53 invalid/ and 4 valid/ cases
options.consequence: G2's generate half fully replayed, at 57 more case directories, four of them with expected/ registries and catalogs that pin more presentation, which every later topics.md change must re-record and review

chosen: rejected/ only, part line for the rest
why: The invalid/ documents already replay against the schema (G1), and nidana.tooling's gates run the generator over valid/ and invalid/; the rejected/ documents are the ones the schema accepts and only the generator rejects (R1 to R4), so they are where a recorded rejection adds the most. The builder half cannot be a recorded invocation without build_runner in a package tree. Signal that would change it: a schema-enforcement regression in the generator reaching nidana.integration despite nidana.tooling's gates.

question: Which ids does each case's Covers cell declare?

options.label: S17's mapping
options.consequence: generate-no-graph G14, G18; each generate-rejected-* G2, G19; generate-graph-undecodable and each generate-usage-* G19

options.label: also G2 on generate-no-graph
options.consequence: declares the acceptance of input/topics.yaml there too, but --guarantee then holds the case back until a phase delivers R1 to R4

chosen: S17's mapping
why: ADR-001 item 9 runs a case only when every id it covers is in the restriction, so an extra id delays a case. The acceptance of input/topics.yaml is already shown by the file replay under G3; the G2 part line says so.

question: State catalog's alignment with nidana-checks@v1's claim recognizer by editing G20, G21 and the Interface bullet in place, or by adding a guarantee G22?

options.label: edit G20, G21 and the bullet in place
options.consequence: one statement per fact, with citations of nidana-checks@v1 G11, G12, G18; the guarantee count stays 21

options.label: add G22
options.consequence: leaves G20 and G21 untouched but restates their claim parts in a third place

chosen: edit G20, G21 and the bullet in place
why: G20 already names the claims and G21 the warnings; the old text deferred to 'the scan nidana-checks@v1 defines', so the edit makes explicit what the reference already bound: unresolvable scopes are left out like unresolvable write sets, stand-in sources keep the claim, an empty write set claims nothing (topology-ir@v1 G12 forbids an empty ShellClaim anyway). The only producer-visible addition is a stderr warning for a site whose scope does not resolve; the document's content rule and every exit code are unchanged, and nidana-checks@v1 G18 already required the same sets. Hence compatible, no stop.

question: Does topic-codegen@v1 pin the form of catalog's stderr warning, for example nidana-checks@v1's warning|unresolved_claim|{site}|{message} line (S16's suggestion), or leave its text unpinned?

options.label: leave the text unpinned
options.consequence: catalog warns once per site with free text; the scan's unresolved_claim line stays the machine-readable report of the same sites (nidana-checks@v1 G18)

options.label: pin nidana-checks@v1's line form
options.consequence: a CI tool could parse catalog's stderr, but the form would be one more not-executable clause (catalog is not replayable while OQ-T1 is open) and catalog's stderr would carry two forms, the line for claims and free text for its exit-1 causes

chosen: leave the text unpinned
why: Nothing reads catalog's stderr today, the scan already gives the machine form over the same sites, and generate's diagnostic message texts are likewise unpinned. Pinning later is a compatible addition. Signal that would change it: a consumer that parses catalog's warnings.

question: A stand-in source names its site relative to the working directory (nidana-checks@v1 G11, G17), so topology-graph.json then depends on where catalog runs. Does topic-codegen@v1 G17 ('the outputs ... hold no timestamp, path or environment value') cover catalog's document, making the alignment a conflict?

options.label: G17 is generate's
options.consequence: the catalog bullet says, citing G17, that unlike generate's outputs a document holding a stand-in depends on the working directory; no guarantee text changes

options.label: G17 covers catalog too
options.consequence: stand-in sources would need a rendering independent of the working directory, which contradicts nidana-checks@v1 G17 and G18 (catalog's claims equal the scan's) and would need a change to that contract

why: G17 is covered in full by the file replay, which runs generate only, and carries no not-executable part for catalog, which ADR-001 item 3 would require if it covered catalog; its 'input files' matches the generate bullet's 'two input files', while catalog reads package directories; only the generate section states the independence. nidana-checks@v1 G18 has bound catalog to the scan's stand-ins since S16, so the dependence exists already and this touch only states it. Signal that would change it: a consumer of topology-graph.json comparing documents produced from different directories.

options.label: diagnostic form only
options.consequence: shorter, but claims G19's 'writes nothing' is replayed for generate-usage-output-is-a-file, where the replay compares no tree but {output} and that case names no {output}

why: ADR-001 item 7 checks 'nothing at {output}' only, and generate-usage-output-is-a-file passes afile as <output>, so whether afile is left unchanged is not observed by the replay.

options.label: bare names at the workspace root
options.consequence: missing.yaml and missing.json, read from the workspace root, which never holds them; the table stays exact and the gate passes

options.label: keep input/missing.*
options.consequence: the gate fails on every run, and a later file of that name under input/ would silently turn the case into a different one

question: Break down nidana.runtime into its child nodes (capability slices within one owner's territory), cut against bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1: which children, of which kind, joined by which contracts, and is an integration child needed?

options.label: Leaf-parent, no children
options.consequence: No internal contract, no ADR change, no integration child; one phase plan of about twelve phases cut along package-internal slices (D2); root D4's clause that calls the runtime internal, the root child table and DAG label change; the step expected children and gets none.

options.label: Two children joined by an internal contract
options.consequence: nidana.runtime.bus (surface, virtual time, delivery, ownership, test support) and nidana.runtime.topology (pipeline, activation, module scopes, barrier and shutdown), about six phases each, acyclic. Needs ADR-001 item 2 amended so an internal contract's fixtures may import lib/src/ (otherwise the contract can never be stable), a second producer of bus-api@v1 whose phase 1 lands nothing of it, one more contract step, and a contract over the read-stage/registry seam that three amendments moved.

options.label: Pure-core child under a shell child
options.consequence: Matches pure core, imperative shell literally, but needs the same ADR-001 amendment and leaves the shell child at about ten phases.

options.label: Live-pipeline or virtual-scheduler child
options.consequence: A node-level cycle with the child that owns the surface (it lands the scheduler's declaration and composes the pipeline, while the sibling's tests need its scheduler), or a second virtual scheduler hand-rolled in the sibling's tests.

chosen: Leaf-parent, no children
why: HSDD's own rules and this tree's accepted ADRs leave no admissible child boundary inside nidana_dart_runtime. (1) TestBus extends the final Bus and VirtualSchedulerProvider the sealed SchedulerProvider, so both contracts' declarations share one library, and ADR-001 item 10 with the fp-progression phase-1 rule puts them in one phase of one leaf-parent. (2) That leaf-parent's surface includes the test substrate every behavior replay runs on, so a scheduler or pipeline sibling forms a cycle with it. (3) Every other sibling needs an internal contract over lib/src/ declarations; ADR-001 item 2 bans src/ imports in fixtures (enforced by the structure set, item 9) and ADR-002 item 3 fixes two public libraries, so that contract can carry no executable validation and hsdd-reconcile can never make it stable (HSDD spec §3.4); the run's --final gate also fails on a non-stable contract. (4) The seam a split would freeze, the interpreter's read stage against the registry's cells, was patched on both sides in three successive experiments (navigation-api-fixtures, bus-api-amendment, bus-api-widened). (5) hsdd-spec's stop-recursing rule holds: one owner (owner's facts) and about twelve phases of one review window each, from a stand-in of about 1,900 lines that passed every suite; hsdd-spec sends a request to break up a node that is already a leaf-parent to hsdd-phase-plan. The tree-shape stop condition does not hold because these stated reasons favor one option. Signal that would have changed my mind: the owner preferring two plans of about six phases to one of about twelve strongly enough to amend ADR-001 item 2 for internal contracts; then the two-children option is the split.
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-api.md Boundary Refinement 1, G2, Validation (bindings run on fresh TestBus instances)
hsdd/conventions.md Phase design (fp-progression: phase 1 lands every declaration of the contracts the node produces)
.agents/skills/hsdd-spec/SKILL.md (Stop recursing; merge when two nodes cannot be tested independently; ambiguous request rule; integration-node rule)

question: With one leaf-parent, how is the package's code divided so phases own disjoint files and the internal mechanisms stay testable apart?

options.label: Slice libraries with package-internal seams
options.consequence: Each slice is its own lib/src/ library reached only through declarations it exposes; the library that declares Bus is the composition root; the pipeline declares its own port, which activation implements on the delivery slice; phases can run in parallel lanes without Collides with; the RxDart engine seam of ADR-002 item 3 is real.

options.label: One library with part files
options.consequence: What every stand-in did: parts share private members, every phase edits one library and serializes behind Collides with, and no slice is testable apart from the others.

options.label: One library per public contract
options.consequence: Ruled out: both contracts share Bus (bus-api@v1 Refinement 1).

chosen: Slice libraries with package-internal seams
why: Disjoint libraries let the phase plan open parallel lanes (the pipeline beside delivery and ownership) and keep each slice unit-testable against the seam it uses, which is the owner's composition-with-explicit-ports practice inside one node; export with show keeps internal names out of application code (bus-testing@v1 G1). No experiment built a stand-in this way; the signal that would change it is a phase finding that a seam forces privates across slices, in which case that pair merges into one library.

question: How do topology reads get their connection before activate returns and every later delivery during that delivery (bus-api@v1 G22, G34), while observed subscriptions keep G17's microtask first delivery?

options.label: Two read paths per cell
options.consequence: Observed subscriptions on the RxDart subject (G17); topology reads on a synchronous broadcast controller with no replay, connection emitted from the current value or buffer before activate returns, connection-caused publishes deferred to a provider-zone microtask.

options.label: Topology reads on the RxDart subject
options.consequence: The replay holds back every delivery made before its first microtask; fails the G34 deep-link case (and G22 when the connection is late).

options.label: Own synchronous subjects for both paths
options.consequence: Gives observed subscriptions a synchronous first value against G17 and rebuilds what Spec §2.3 expects the engine to provide.

chosen: Two read paths per cell
why: It is the only shape that passed every suite in the experiments after the S13 amendment; S13 asked the decomposition for exactly this.

question: How does the registry represent a topic reached through a widened reference and at its value type in either order (bus-api@v1 G41)?

options.label: Cells at Object? with per-access conversion
options.consequence: Values, buffers, subject elements and envelopes held at Object?; each access converts at its own type argument; envelopes never cast to MessageEnvelope<T>; writers per (topic, type argument); collision check on declaration fields.

options.label: Typed cells through a topic-model@v1 type-capturing member
options.consequence: Typed envelopes and a publish-time value check, but needs a compatible topic-model@v1 addition nobody requested.

chosen: Cells at Object? with per-access conversion
why: topic-model@v1 gives generic code no way to instantiate at a topic's value type from a widened reference; the patched stand-in built this way passed every suite, and typed cells failed the six G41 cases. Signal to change: an adopter who needs typed envelopes from widened publishes.

question: Where does the TypeError go when an off-type value published through a widened reference fails one subscription's or read's conversion, so it never stops delivery to the others (bus-api@v1 G13)?

options.label: Provider zone's uncaught-error handler, value skipped there
options.consequence: Conversion runs in that subscription's or read's own delivery callback; the failing one skips the value and keeps receiving; recorders, observers and every other subscription and read receive the delivery; a conversion at a call (getCurrentValue, getBufferedValues, a reduceInto seed in activate) throws to the caller; consistent with G18's throwing-callback rule.

options.label: Error event on the subscription and at the read stage
options.consequence: Ends an observed subscription that sets cancelOnError, and ends every sink downstream of the read (G26) for a value the topology cannot control.

options.label: Publish-time check
options.consequence: Needs the typed-cell alternative of D4 and its topic-model@v1 addition.

chosen: Provider zone's uncaught-error handler, value skipped there
why: The experiment shows a cast in one listener's onData reaches the zone handler while the listeners before and after it receive the value, add() returns normally and the failing listener gets the next value; it matches what G18 already says for a throwing callback. A consumer could rely on it, so the phase plan may emit it as a compatible amend to G41's exclusion. Signal to change: the owner wanting off-type publishes surfaced as a dev-mode diagnostic, which would add a BusDiagnostic variant, a breaking change to bus-api@v1.

question: Routed amend, bus-testing@v1 G16: what do envelopesOf and payloadsOf return for an envelope published through a widened reference (a MessageEnvelope<Object?>, which cannot be both typed by the topic and identical)?

options.label: Equal rebuilt envelope when not a MessageEnvelope<T>
options.consequence: The delivered envelope itself when it is a MessageEnvelope<T>, else an equal MessageEnvelope<T> built from its eight fields with the payload converted; payloadsOf converts payloads; an off-type payload throws TypeError from the query; == comparisons hold, only identical differs.

options.label: Skip such records
options.consequence: Silently drops deliveries a test asserts on.

options.label: Throw for such records
options.consequence: A test of generic shell code could never read its topic.

options.label: Typed envelopes at publish
options.consequence: Needs D4's alternative (a topic-model@v1 type-capturing member).

chosen: Equal rebuilt envelope when not a MessageEnvelope<T>
why: topic-model@v1's public constructor takes all eight fields and equality is field-wise, so the rebuilt envelope is equal to the delivered one; bus-testing@v1's stated assertion API is ==; identity is kept wherever G16 could keep it before, and where it could not the stand-in threw. nidana.runtime's phase plan emits it as amend bus-testing@v1 (G16).
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-testing.md G16, How a test uses it

question: Routed amend, bus-testing@v1 G18: how does TestBus.stub return 'the same writer on every later call' when calls come at different type arguments?

options.label: One publisher per topic, writer per type argument
options.consequence: The first call for a topic at any type argument creates one testSource publisher claiming it; stub<T> returns that publisher's writer<T>, the same handle per type argument (bus-api@v1 G20, G41); amend text: 'the same writer on every later call with the same type argument'.

options.label: One cached writer cast per call
options.consequence: Fails at run time (StateWriter<Object?> cast to StateWriter<int>).

options.label: A publisher per type argument
options.consequence: The second claim on one topic is a second writer, rejected by bus-api@v1 G20 with ClaimRejected.

chosen: One publisher per topic, writer per type argument
why: The other two options fail; this one matches bus-api@v1 G20's per-type-argument wording. nidana.runtime's phase plan emits it as amend bus-testing@v1 (G18).

question: S22 reversed root D4: nidana.runtime becomes a leaf-parent (about twelve phases over ten internal slices) instead of an internal node with children. The two leading options (leaf-parent; or two children nidana.runtime.bus and nidana.runtime.topology joined by an internal contract) produce different nodes and contracts, and the Specification is silent. Is this the tree-shape run-stop?

options.label: Not a stop; accept the leaf-parent

why: The experiment reproduces both observations with one probe plugin on the pinned analyzer 13.3.0 and analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18. A diagnostic reports at the severity the plugin's diagnostics section configures for its code, otherwise at the severity its LintCode declares; LintCode's constructor defaults that to INFO. registerWarningRule versus registerLintRule decides only default enablement, and the reported type is always STATIC_WARNING. The workspace-layout stand-ins construct LintCode with no severity (hence INFO); the nidana-checks-fixtures stand-in passes severity: DiagnosticSeverity.WARNING for three codes and nothing for unflagged_sensitive_topic (hence WARNING and INFO). So ADR-002 generalized a property of its stand-in into a property of plugins. nidana-checks@v1 G1 is achievable as written and agrees with the observed exit codes (C3: INFO exits 0, 1 under --fatal-infos; C4: WARNING exits 2; C5: ERROR exits 3).
