options.consequence: One diff for shutdown, but 66 of 95 bus-api@v1 cases and 23 of 45 bus-testing@v1 cases call start(), and bus-api@v1 G8, G18 and bus-testing@v1 G5, G9, G14, G17, G18 call shutdown(), so almost no behavior replays before the last phase.

chosen: start with the publish path, shutdown incremental (D8)
why: The suites cannot replay delivery without start(), and several non-lifecycle guarantees assert on shutdown; incremental teardown keeps each slice's shutdown with the code that owns the resource. Recorded as D8. Signal that would change it: a reviewer who wants all of shutdown in one diff.

question: How do gates check bus-api@v1 G38, G39 and bus-testing@v1 G20 ('checked by nidana.runtime's gates'), given that every gate must be an fvm command?

options.label: Package test plus one provider library (D9)
options.consequence: A test in packages/nidana_dart_runtime/test checks the pubspec and the sources; every timer and microtask goes through one internal provider library, so the check can forbid Timer( and the global scheduleMicrotask( elsewhere; the pipeline gets its timer through its port.

options.label: grep in each gate
options.consequence: Not an fvm command, not run with the package's tests.

options.label: Review only
options.consequence: zone.run at each call site cannot be told apart from a timer outside the zone by a source check.

chosen: Package test plus one provider library (D9)
why: ADR-003 Consequences anticipates a source search for DateTime.now(, Stopwatch( and timers outside the provider implementation; a Dart test keeps the gate an fvm command, and model-gate-commands showed fvm dart test packages/{member} runs from the workspace root. Recorded as D9.

question: Is the delivery slice one phase or several?

options.label: Pure core, registry and cells, publish path; ownership separate
options.consequence: Four phases of about 330 to 420 lines each (nidana.runtime.2, .6, .7, .8); .6 replays no guarantee of its own because its cases publish through publishers.

options.label: One delivery phase plus ownership
options.consequence: About 850 lines, two PEs in one review sitting.

chosen: Pure core, registry and cells, publish path; ownership separate
why: The stand-in's registry, cells, publish path, observers and recorder seam are about 400 lines without docs or tests (docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-widened/packages/nidana_dart_runtime/lib/src/bus.dart); the PE ceiling forces the split.

question: Is the pipeline one phase or two?

options.label: Two phases
options.consequence: Synchronous stages and sinks first (.9), then switchMap, retry, time stages and cancellation (.10), which need the virtual scheduler.

options.label: One phase
options.consequence: About 750 lines with tests; one review sitting cannot hold it.

chosen: Two phases
why: The stand-in interpreter alone is 438 lines; the split follows ADR-003 items 3 and 4, which govern the second half only.

question: Is activation one phase or two?

options.label: Checks and handles, then wiring
options.consequence: nidana.runtime.11 (planOf, idempotency, limits, analyses, handles, ownership, live graph, activation observers) runs beside the pipeline lane; nidana.runtime.12 implements the port and the connection timing and binds the live suite. Each replays guarantees of its own.

options.label: One activation phase
options.consequence: About 660 lines and 8 or more tasks, above the PE; the connection timing reviewed together with the checks.

chosen: Checks and handles, then wiring
why: Merged it exceeds the PE; the read path's timing (D3) is the seam that moved most in the experiments (D1 point 4), which is a stated reason to review it in isolation. The fixtures confirm the split has replay value: G1, G10, G20, G21, G24, G32, G37 pass without wiring.

question: Where do the small slices go: telemetry (about 100 lines) and the residual lifecycle (startup window, onShutdown, G36 order)?

options.label: Telemetry with test support, lifecycle with module scopes
options.consequence: Two phases of about 330 and 400 lines; each pair is a sizing-floor merge (same tier, no third phase needs one without the other).

options.label: Separate phases
options.consequence: Two phases below the floor whose process artifacts would exceed their diffs.

chosen: Telemetry with test support, lifecycle with module scopes
why: The sizing floor: a phase must earn its cycle; telemetry alone and the residual lifecycle alone do not. Signal that would change it: a separate owner for observability.

question: When does a guarantee join a producing gate's --guarantee list?

options.label: When every case of it can pass
options.consequence: Lists derived case by case from the fixtures; several guarantees replay later than the phase that implements their slice (delivery guarantees from the ownership phase on).

options.label: When its slice lands
options.consequence: Gates would fail: most cases publish through publishers, call start(), or activate a topology.

chosen: When every case of it can pass
why: ADR-001 item 10 restricts behavior to the guarantees delivered so far, and a gate must pass; a case runs only when every id it covers is in the restriction (item 9). The derivation is mechanical and reproducible.

question: How are producing phases' gates written: 'node default plus' the replay, or the full command?

options.label: Full command per producing phase
options.consequence: Each producing phase's Gate is a complete fvm chain; hsdd-config copies it verbatim into the phase context and the superpowers derivative.

options.label: node default plus replay
options.consequence: Shorter, but hsdd-config replaces only a Gate that is exactly 'node default', so the context could carry an unresolved phrase.

chosen: Full command per producing phase
why: hsdd-config's switch rule resolves 'node default' only as the whole Gate value; the full command avoids an implementing session guessing the default.
evidence: .agents/skills/hsdd-config/SKILL.md (The Generic Phase Context, The Superpowers Derivative)

question: How are the pipeline phases verified before activation composes them?

options.label: Unit tests against a port of the test's own
options.consequence: As D2 and the Isolation strategy state; the live suite replays through Bus.activate from the wiring phase on.

options.label: Bind the live suite to a test-local mini bus
options.consequence: Earlier coverage of topology-dsl@v1 G18 to G29, but the harness would re-implement delivery, dedup and reentrancy in test code, about 150 to 200 lines more per phase.

chosen: Unit tests against a port of the test's own
why: D2 already decided it; a test-local bus that passes the live suite is a second runtime to maintain. Signal that would change it: a pipeline defect that the unit tests missed and the live suite caught at the wiring phase.

question: Does the pipeline reuse the delivery core's per-read dedup state, making nidana.runtime.9 depend on nidana.runtime.2?

options.label: Reuse the delivery core's dedup
options.consequence: One implementation for observed subscriptions and topology reads (bus-api@v1 G16, topology-dsl@v1 G19); .9 waits on .2.

options.label: Pipeline's own dedup
options.consequence: .9 depends only on the package; two implementations of one rule.

chosen: Reuse the delivery core's dedup
why: G16 and live G19 state the same rule; one function keeps them from drifting, and .2 is an early pure phase, so the wait is short.

question: Does test support and telemetry (nidana.runtime.13) wait on activation wiring, or run beside it after ownership with a smaller replay?

options.label: Wait on activation wiring
options.consequence: Its gate replays bus-testing@v1 G3, G12 to G19 and bus-api@v1 G33, whose cases activate topologies; serial anyway, since both edit lib/src/bus.dart.

options.label: Run beside activation
options.consequence: Its gate could replay only bus-testing@v1 G15 and G16; the rest would join at a later gate, and the two phases would still serialize on bus.dart.

chosen: Wait on activation wiring
why: The collision on bus.dart (TestBus) serializes them regardless; waiting lets the phase replay what it delivers.

question: Which phases are listed as producing bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1?

options.label: Phases that implement public members
options.consequence: bus-api@v1 [.1, .5, .6, .7, .8, .11, .12, .13, .14], bus-testing@v1 [.1, .5, .7, .13, .14]; .6 and .7 produce members whose guarantees replay later; pure and pipeline phases produce none.

options.label: Phases that add a replayed guarantee
options.consequence: Drops .6 and bus-testing's .7, hiding where observe, getCurrentValue and the recorder seam are implemented.

chosen: Phases that implement public members
why: Reconcile writes the Delivery paragraph from the confirms and the gates' lists; naming the implementing phases and saying when their guarantees replay tells consumers both facts.

question: Phase 1 is above the ~400-line PE (about 420 lines). Split it?

options.label: Keep one phase
options.consequence: Gate-only, mostly declarations and doc comments; the replay checks it mechanically.

options.label: Split
options.consequence: ADR-001 item 10 runs surface and reject in full from the first producing phase, so each contract's declarations must land in one phase, and the two contracts share a library (D1 point 1).

chosen: Keep one phase
why: The split is not allowed by ADR-001 item 10; the overage is small and declaration-heavy.

question: Review tiers for the effect phases: full-review throughout, or spot-check for the ownership phase?

options.label: full-review for every effect phase but test support
options.consequence: Ownership (single-writer enforcement), delivery timing, activation and the scheduler are business logic and orchestration; test support and telemetry are well constrained by their suites.

options.label: spot-check for ownership
options.consequence: Lighter review of the claims check, which enforces Spec §3.11 layer 1.

chosen: full-review for every effect phase but test support
why: The skill puts orchestration and business logic at full-review; single-writer enforcement is a guarantee consumers rely on for correctness.

question: amend bus-api@v1 G41's outside clause per D5: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: The clause stated no behavior for an off-type value; nothing changes for a value of the topic's value type.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

chosen: Compatible
why: It adds behavior where the contract was silent, and no fixture of any contract publishes an off-type value; evidence in docs/auto-run/experiments/off-type-delivery/.

question: amend bus-testing@v1 G16 per D6: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: Identity holds wherever G16 could hold it; only a widened envelope gets an equal copy where the old wording threw.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

chosen: Compatible
why: Probe P2 showed the earlier wording threw a TypeError for exactly the case that changes; == comparisons hold in both cases.

question: amend bus-testing@v1 G18 per D7: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: Only calls for one topic at two type arguments change, where the old wording could not hold; one publisher per topic keeps one claim.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

chosen: Compatible
why: T7 in bus-api-widened showed the old wording fails at run time for that case.

question: S30's gates nidana.runtime.5 to .11 assume the replay tool passes bus_activation_test.dart (bus-api@v1's binding of topology-dsl@v1's live suite) when no case of it falls within --guarantee. Does that agree with nidana.model D2, or is it a request-style assumption conflicting with another node's entry (a collision)?

options.label: agree
options.consequence: No collision. D2 item 4 (a slug's behavior cases run only as the restriction admits them; a slug with no id in the restriction runs none of them) and ADR-001 item 9 (a bare G{n} is the replayed slug's; the tool learns a binding's suite from the conformance library it imports; a case runs only when every id it covers is in the restriction) leave the live binding with no admitted case at .5 to .11, and D2 item 1 fails a run only on a failing or PENDING fixture. The two implementation hazards the experiment shows go to the hsdd-adr clarification of ADR-001 item 9 already recommended at S29.

options.label: disagree
options.consequence: A collision: stop before applying anything; the orchestrator would arbitrate between changing nidana.runtime's gates and changing nidana.model's tool semantics.

chosen: agree
why: Both texts make an excluded case not run and neither makes an empty selection a failure or a usage error; nidana.model.6's scope adds 'a slug with no id in the restriction runs no binding'. Read with ADR-001 item 9, the slug that matters for a binding is the slug of the suite it imports (topology-dsl), which has no id at .5 to .11. The experiment found two ways a tool could still fail the gates, neither of which D2 permits: dart test exits 79 ('No tests ran') when the name filter admits nothing (E2), and nidana.runtime.11's bare bus-api ids used as a raw name filter would run topology-dsl's same-numbered live cases G18 to G21, G24 and G29 before the pipeline is wired (E3). The per-binding empty case is implied rather than stated, hence medium confidence. The signal that would have changed my mind: D2 or nidana.model.6 stating that a binding whose filter admits no case is run anyway, or is an error.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D2 items 1 and 4, nidana.model.6 Scope

question: bus-testing@v1's consumers frontmatter is [nidana.navigation, nidana.flutter, nidana.integration], while nidana.runtime's Contracts table (S26 finding) and S30's confirm sub-bullet name nidana.tooling as a contract-edge consumer. Add nidana.tooling now, or wait for its plan's confirm?

options.label: wait for its confirm entry
options.consequence: The frontmatter stays one consumer short until nidana.tooling.lint's plan is reconciled; the Delivery paragraph already names nidana.tooling's edge; no reconcile writes a consumer no plan emitted (S29's precedent for topology-ir@v1).

options.label: add nidana.tooling now
options.consequence: Matches the spec tables at once, but writes a consumers entry no pending section carries, outside step 4's rule.

chosen: wait for its confirm entry
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 applies confirm entries only, and the consumer is nidana.tooling.lint, whose plan will confirm phase ids. phase_ids stays provisional either way.

question: How do nidana.runtime's consumer confirms land in the three model contracts' consumers lists: replace the node id with the confirmed phase ids, or keep the node id?

options.label: replace the node id with its phase ids
options.consequence: consumers lists nidana.runtime.1 to .14 as confirmed (13, 6 and 3 ids) beside the unplanned node ids; the registry's consumer count becomes 17, 10 and 5 entries, not nodes.

options.label: keep the node id
options.consequence: The registry count stays a node count, but the confirm is not applied and hsdd-contract's gate 'consumers lists phase ids that actually consume this contract' fails for a planned consumer.

chosen: replace the node id with its phase ids
why: hsdd-contract's quality gate asks for phase ids, the step prompt says the contracts gain nidana.runtime's consumer phase ids, and produced_by already carries phase ids since S29. The count change in INDEX.md is derived data.

question: The three behavioral amends (bus-api@v1 G41 off-type clause, bus-testing@v1 G16, bus-testing@v1 G18) add behavior their existing cases do not reach. Cover them with new cases in this edit, or apply the body changes with not-executable lines and schedule an hsdd-contract step?

options.label: five new cases now
options.consequence: Three G41 cases (observed subscriptions, conversions at a call with the reduceInto seed and activate's rollback, topology reads at connection and later delivery), one G16 case, one G18 case; checked against a stand-in patched for D5 to D7, against the unpatched stand-in and against seeded defects; no follow-up step.

options.label: not-executable lines and an hsdd-contract step
options.consequence: Faster here, but a behavior that can be executed is recorded as not executable until a later step adds the cases.

chosen: five new cases now
why: The step prompt prefers fixtures when the work is a few cases, and the stand-in of docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-widened/ needed a patch of four small hunks. Results: every suite that imports nidana_dart_runtime passes on the patched stand-in (bus-api 98/98, live 43/43, bus-testing 47/47, navigation 40/40 and 52/52, flutter-binding 52/52 and 26/26); on the unpatched stand-in exactly four of the five new cases fail (the observed-subscription case passes there, since that stand-in already converted in the subscriber's callback); five seeded defects each fail the case of what they break; both structure prototypes pass. No reject fixture changed, so no reject code needed confirming. The new cases join the --guarantee lists S30 already scheduled (G41 at nidana.runtime.12, G16 and G18 at nidana.runtime.13).

question: The G41 amend makes getCurrentValue and getBufferedValues throw TypeError at the call for an off-type value, while G8 says 'neither throws except TopicCollision'. Is the amend still compatible, and what happens to G8?

options.label: compatible; G8 names the TypeError
options.consequence: G41 gains the off-type clause and G8 reads 'neither throws except TopicCollision, or the TypeError G41 states for a value that is not of the topic's value type'; v1 kept with a Versioning line.

options.label: breaking; stop for the owner
options.consequence: The run stops until the orchestrator decides whether to bump bus-api to v2 or drop the amend.

options.label: apply G41 only
options.consequence: The contract reads as self-contradictory between G8 and G41.

chosen: compatible; G8 names the TypeError
why: Before the amend no behavior conformed to G8 for an off-type current value: G8 also says getCurrentValue is the last value delivered, which is not of the type the call returns, and topic-model@v1 offers generic code no way to check a value against a topic's type at publish (nidana.runtime D4, D5), so an implementation could only throw or return a value G8 does not allow. No consumer can have relied on a no-throw result. flutter-binding@v1 G5 builds from getCurrentValue but states nothing for an off-type value, and no fixture of any contract publishes one. A careful engineer might still have shown the owner the G8 edit, since it touches a throw statement the Breaking list names. The signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer contract or fixture expecting a fallback value for an off-type current value.

question: The amend entry says each conversion runs 'in the delivery callback of the one subscription or topology read it serves' and lists the conversions made at a call. A read's connection is converted during activate. Does the G41 text say which rule covers it?

options.label: state the connection explicitly
options.consequence: G41 says 'its first values and a read's connection included'; an off-type connection value goes to the provider zone's handler and activate returns normally; case three pins it.

options.label: keep the entry's wording
options.consequence: A reader could take the connection for a conversion made during activate and expect activate to throw, which nidana.runtime.12's scope does not do.

chosen: state the connection explicitly
why: D4 has every topology read convert each payload and nidana.runtime.12's scope converts 'each value' in the read's own callback, connection values included; only the reduceInto seed throws to the caller. Saying so removes the one ambiguity a consumer could build on. The signal that would have changed my mind: a plan text that throws from activate for an off-type connection value.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.runtime.md D3, D4, D5, nidana.runtime.12 Scope

question: In the Delivery paragraphs, does 'phase X delivers G{n}' name the phase whose gate first replays the guarantee or the phase that implements its slice?

options.label: the phase that first replays it
options.consequence: Consumers wait for a guarantee whose cases pass at a producing gate; nidana.runtime.6 (registry, cells, observed streams) and nidana.runtime.7 (bus-testing@v1's recorder seam) are named as implementing phases whose guarantees replay later.

options.label: the phase that implements its slice
options.consequence: Earlier dates, but a consumer could build on a guarantee no gate has checked yet.

chosen: the phase that first replays it
why: The conventions' Contracts paragraph reads delivery from the plan's entries and its gates' --guarantee lists, and S30's confirm sub-bullets list the replay phases, naming .6 and .7 separately. The paragraphs also carry note 4: G38, G39 and bus-testing@v1 G20 are checked by packages/nidana_dart_runtime/test/package_properties_test.dart, because the not-executable line format ('checked by {node}'s gates') is ADR-001's and parsed by the structure set.

question: topology-dsl@v1's Delivery paragraph says G18 to G29 'are the live implementation's'. Does it gain the phase that delivers them, which S30's topology-dsl confirm sub-bullet states (replayed from nidana.runtime.12 on)?

options.label: add the phase
options.consequence: Consumers of topology-dsl@v1's live semantics (navigation, flutter, integration) read that nidana.runtime implements them and that they replay from nidana.runtime.12, pointing at bus-api@v1's Delivery.

options.label: leave the paragraph
options.consequence: Those consumers would have to find the date in bus-api@v1, a contract some of them do not consume through a contract edge.

chosen: add the phase
why: The convention puts which producing phase delivers which guarantees in the contract a consumer reads; for G18 to G29 the producing node is nidana.runtime, not the produced_by nidana.model phases. One clause, no guarantee changes.

question: The drained entries resolve no OQ, but two citations of OQ-R1 (RESOLVED 2026-10-17 by bus-api@v1 G17) still read as open: ADR-003 item 6 'whichever first-delivery timing OQ-R1 gives', and nidana.flutter's 'a new observe subscription may receive its first value one microtask later'. Sweep them now?

options.label: sweep both
options.consequence: Both cite bus-api@v1 G17 as the resolution and state the timing; no decision, item or link changes; the quality gate 'no artifact still cites a resolved OQ as open' holds.

options.label: leave them
options.consequence: The sweep stays limited to OQs this drain resolves, and the two stale citations survive until another reconcile or the owners' next touch.

chosen: sweep both
why: OQ-R1 belongs to the node being drained, the skill's quality gate is tree-wide, and the step allows an ADR edit for step 13's citation sweep. S29 swept ADR-003's OQ-M3 line the same way, without an Amendments entry.

question: note 1 (nidana.runtime.1 is the node's only member-creating phase; the conventions' 'one phase each of nidana.runtime' is nidana.runtime.1): does it change a convention?

options.label: no change
options.consequence: The Shared workspace files bullet stays as written; the rule already covers nidana.runtime.1, and the plan's scope carries the phase id.

options.label: name nidana.runtime.1 in the bullet
options.consequence: The bullet names a planned phase for the runtime as it does for nidana.model, but reconcile writes a plan fact into the conventions without a rule change.

chosen: no change
why: hsdd-reconcile step 10 applies a note only when it changes a convention and drops derived facts; the note confirms the plan follows the rule. Notes 2 (replay sets used) and 3 (empty selection) change no convention either: note 2 restates the Phase design bullet, and note 3 is tool behavior that ADR-001 item 9 and nidana.model D2 own. The signal that would have changed my mind: an executor of another node needing the runtime's member-creating phase id and having no other place to read it.

question: While applying the G41 amend, S31 edited bus-api@v1 G8 ('neither throws except TopicCollision') so it also names G41's TypeError for an off-type value, and flagged it as a possible breaking amend. Is it the breaking-amend run-stop?

options.label: Not a stop; keep the edit
options.consequence: G8 and G41 agree; the stand-in experiment shows every suite that imports nidana_dart_runtime still passes.

options.label: Stop the run
options.consequence: The owner decides a wording change to a guarantee that no implementation could meet as written.

chosen: Not a stop; keep the edit
why: The breaking-amend stop guards an existing consumer. No consumer code exists, and before the edit G8 could not be satisfied for an off-type value at all, because G41 already required the TypeError; the edit removes a contradiction rather than taking a promise away. Every consuming contract's fixtures pass against the amended stand-in (docs/auto-run/experiments/runtime-reconcile-amends/).

question: navigation-api@v1 G13 fixes the nav-resolver's edges and order but not the functions they record; topology-ir@v1 G9 leaves a closure anonymous. Should the template's two stage functions be closures or named method tear-offs?

options.label: method tear-offs of private stage classes
options.consequence: The recorded IR and every rendered graph name the stages resolveDeepLinks and applyAuthGuard, as Guide §3.4 draws them; about 35 more lines; consumers can see the names, so a compatible amend of G13 goes to reconcile and hsdd-contract adds an assertion or a not-executable line.

options.label: closures
options.consequence: No extra code and no amend, but two of the resolver's three transforms render as (anonymous) in bus.toGraph(), the catalog and the JSON form.

chosen: method tear-offs of private stage classes
why: Spec §6.2 asks for named transformers and Spec §6.5 treats a topology as self-documenting data; the experiment shows tear-offs record the names in both forms, keep two resolvers of one configuration equal, and pass all 40 navigation cases and 52 executor registrations unchanged. Because the names are visible across the boundary the choice is emitted as an amend rather than kept node-local.

question: How to cut nidana.navigation into phases under fp-progression: where the resolver template and resultsFor go, and whether the in-memory router stands alone.

options.label: six phases, template with the guard
options.consequence: Declarations; values; access, guard and resolver template (full-review, ~400 lines); executor values and planner; in-memory router; executor and live wiring. The security chain (guard table plus resolve-before-guard order) is reviewed in one sitting; the guard work waits on nidana.model.11 for its G13 replay.

options.label: seven phases, template in its own phase
options.consequence: A spot-check template phase of about 180 lines that could run beside the values and planner lanes as soon as nidana.model.11 merges; one more cycle whose process artifacts would rival its diff, and the guard and the stage order reviewed apart.

options.label: five phases, router folded into the planner
options.consequence: One cycle fewer, but the merged phase comes to about 500 lines, over the review window, and mixes the pure band with the effect band.

chosen: six phases, template with the guard
why: The template alone sits below the sizing floor, and the guard and the template's stage order together are one security property (navigation-api@v1 Refinement 3), so reviewing them together in one full-review phase buys more than the parallel lane. resultsFor rides with the template because both are recorded DSL compositions. The signal that would have favored seven phases: nidana.model.11 expected to land much later than nidana.model.8, holding up the guard work.

question: Review tier of nidana.navigation.3 (access values, resolveDeepLinks, applyAuthGuard, navResolver, resultsFor), a mostly pure phase.

options.label: full-review
options.consequence: A full design and verification doc and a diff read for a pure phase; the guard table and the stage order get edge-case review.

options.label: spot-check
options.consequence: Cheaper review of well-constrained pure functions with exhaustive fixture cases; a subtle guard or order error relies on the fixtures alone.

chosen: full-review
why: The phase decides access: an error in G12's table or in the template's stage order opens a protected route, the bypass navigation-api@v1 Refinement 3 exists to close. The tier table puts security at full-review.

question: Where do the live resolver replays (G14, G16) land: with the resolver template, or in the final phase with the executor?

options.label: final phase
options.consequence: The template phase stays pure and waits on nothing later than nidana.model.11; G14 and G16 replay once, at nidana.navigation.6, which waits on nidana.runtime.14 anyway.

options.label: with the template
options.consequence: The template phase would wait on nidana.runtime.14, the hard edge, putting a pure phase on the critical path after the runtime ships.

chosen: final phase
why: --guarantee selects by guarantee id, and G16 has one recorded and one live case, so G16 cannot replay before a real TestBus exists; G14 is all live. The template adds no code for live behavior, which is the runtime's interpretation of the recorded plan. Keeping nidana.navigation.1 to .5 off nidana.runtime.14 lets them merge while the runtime's later phases run.
evidence: ADR-001 item 9 (--guarantee restricts behavior cases by name prefix)

question: Which phase replays G9 (the five topic declarations, complete at nidana.navigation.1), whose case needs topic-model@v1's values from nidana.model.8?

options.label: nidana.navigation.3
options.consequence: nidana.navigation.2 starts after nidana.model.6 alone; nidana.navigation.3 already needs nidana.model.8 for G13's TopicRef comparisons.

options.label: nidana.navigation.2
options.consequence: The topics replay one phase earlier, but nidana.navigation.2 and everything after it wait on nidana.model.8.

chosen: nidana.navigation.3
why: It removes a cross-node wait from nidana.navigation.2 at no cost, since nidana.navigation.3 depends on nidana.model.8 for G13 regardless.
evidence: topic-model@v1 Delivery (nidana.model.8 delivers every behavior guarantee)

question: Should the executor and the live composition (G14, G15, G16, G24 and the bootstrap test) be one phase or two?

options.label: one phase
options.consequence: About 360 lines (100 of library code), 7 plan tasks, full-review; nidana.flutter's binding of the executor suite waits on one phase.

options.label: two phases
options.consequence: An executor phase and a live-wiring phase that writes almost no library code; the second's process artifacts would exceed its diff, and flutter's G24 replay would wait on a later phase than G18 to G23.
